asked_by: Ace, 2026-10-31: the next research problem is how scores translate into trade value and admission priority; execute until the issue is narrower or resolved; no strategy changes
status: attribution study on 2023 (already-studied data), simulation only; not investable, not a strategy, no permission to buy; 2024 data never read; any threshold or priority rule the curves suggest is a hypothesis for a fresh period, not a result
candidates: every eligible 2023 early-population coin-day scored with the frozen coefficients and temperatures (no fitting); the top five per day must reproduce CRYPTO_REPLAY_v1's pinned shortlists

isolated_trade.who: every candidate with predicted upside probability >= 5% under any arm, plus every shortlisted alert
isolated_trade.engine: idxsig.crypto_replay.run, one alert, CRYPTO_REPLAY_v1 BASE policy, equity 10,000

analyses:
A  calibration: realized hit rate by predicted-probability bin on all early candidates, per arm; the shortlist's
     mean predicted probability against its realized hit rate
  B  global threshold curve: candidates with p >= t (any day, no budget): count, days, hit rate, mean and median
     isolated net return, and the same on first alerts of consecutive-day runs
  C  admission timing: isolated outcomes of all five alerts on days the account could admit versus days it could not
  D  rank anatomy: predicted p, repeat share, volatility, hit rate and isolated net by rank 1..5
  E  value accounting: EV per alert = P(hit) x net(hit) + P(non-hit) x net(non-hit); the EV the predicted
     probabilities implied; the hit rate needed for 1% net per trade at the observed payoffs

verdict_rules.calibration: OVERCONFIDENT AT THE TOP if, in every bin that holds shortlisted alerts, the realized hit rate is below half the bin's mean predicted probability, in both model arms
verdict_rules.threshold: reported for every threshold; a level is called PROMISING only if its mean isolated net return is >= 1.0% with >= 100 candidates in the year, in both model arms; promising means test it on a fresh period, nothing more
verdict_rules.timing: ENTERS AT BAD TIMES if, in both model arms, the five alerts on days the account admitted something average a lower isolated net return than on days it admitted nothing, with the signal-day bootstrap interval of the difference below zero
